summary: A devbox in a terminal state permanently wedges the LRU: reserveCapacity re-picks it as the suspend candidate, suspendRecord throws every time, and no new room can ever provision until server restart.
failure_scenario: Room A's devbox hits 'failure' during startup (waitForDevbox throws at line 357-359) or auto-shuts down after the 4h keep_alive. The catch at lines 741-747 keeps the record active because devboxId is set. Later, with capacity full (e.g. pinned demo room + this dead record = maxLive 2), any new room enters the while loop at line 507; the dead record passes the candidate filter (status 'error', has devboxId, not provisioning), suspendRecord POSTs /suspend on a shutdown/failed devbox which returns 4xx (or waitForDevbox sees the terminal state and throws at line 356-359). The error propagates, the new room's provision fails — and the poisoned record is never cleared, so EVERY subsequent room creation and every retry of room A fails identically for the rest of the night.
suggested_fix: In reserveCapacity, wrap `await suspendRecord(candidate, "lru", ...)` in try/catch: on failure, mark candidate.active = false (and log) so the loop makes progress — a devbox that can't be suspended is effectively gone anyway. Additionally, in suspendRecord, treat a RunloopRequestError 4xx or a terminal-state result as 'already inactive' (set active=false, return) instead of throwing.

verdict.reason: Verified end-to-end in provision.mjs and caller index.js; every refutation attempt failed. (1) The catch at lines 741-747 keeps a failed record active whenever devboxId is set (assigned at line 599, before all failure-prone steps). (2) suspendRecord on a terminal devbox always throws: POST /suspend 4xx throws at line 333, and a non-suspended 2xx leads to waitForDevbox returning the terminal status and throwing at 356-359; record.active=false (line 478) is unreachable on failure, so the candidate is never cleared. (3) The dead record's frozen lastUsedAt makes it deterministically the LRU candidate at line 527 on every attempt, while the pinned demo record (registerPinned, index.js 1555) is filter-excluded and permanently holds the other maxLive=2 slot. (4) No recovery exists: index.js's provision catch only emits a status; release() runs only on manual DELETE /rooms/:roomId with a steer key; retrying the dead room throws identically via lines 503-505. Only narrowing caveat: common mid-provision failures (npm/Vite/clone errors) leave a running devbox that suspends fine — the wedge requires a terminal devbox (Runloop boot failure, the 4h keep_alive expiry at line 595, or manual shutdown), which is realistic tonight for a room created hours before the demo. Once triggered, all room creation fails until server restart — demo-breaking, and the suggested one-line try/catch fix is sound.

summary: Creating a second room while another is still provisioning hard-fails with 'capacity is full' instead of waiting, because in-flight records are excluded from suspension candidates.
failure_scenario: maxLive defaults to 2 and the pinned demo room permanently occupies one active slot. Provisioning takes minutes (devbox boot + npm install + vite health). A judge or teammate creates room B while room A is mid-provision: activeRecords() = [pinned demo, A(provisioning)] >= 2, the candidate filter at lines 509-515 excludes both (pinned / status 'provisioning'), and line 523 throws immediately. The user sees workspace.status error for room B even though nothing is actually wrong — extremely likely during live demo where rooms get created back-to-back.
suggested_fix: Before throwing at line 522-526, if any inflight provisions exist, `await Promise.allSettled([...inflight.values()])` (outside the capacity queue, or via a bounded wait/retry loop) and re-evaluate candidates; only throw when there genuinely is no record that can ever be suspended. Alternatively raise maxLive or surface a 'queued, waiting for a free workspace slot' status instead of an error.

verdict.reason: Confirmed against the deployed configuration. Production runs buildServer() with no options, so maxLive = 2 (index.js:394, 1628), and both deploy scripts set DEMO_ROOM=1 with DEMO_WORKSPACE_JSON, so registerPinned("demo") creates a permanently active, never-suspendable pinned record occupying one slot (index.js:1555; provision.mjs registerPinned sets active:true/pinned:true, and both the candidate filter and suspendRecord exclude pinned records). When room A is created, reserveCapacity inserts its record with status "provisioning" and releases the capacity queue immediately; status stays "provisioning" for the entire multi-minute provision (devbox boot wait, npm install, vite health polling) until line 723. If room B is created in that window, activeRecords() = [demo(pinned), A(provisioning)] >= 2, the candidate filter at provision.mjs:508-515 excludes both (pinned / status "provisioning" / null devboxId), and the while loop throws immediately at lines 522-526 with no await on inflight, no retry, and no queueing. The error propagates as workspace.status "error" to room B's clients, B's record is deleted, and nothing re-triggers provisioning (initializeRoom runs once per POST /rooms). Every built-in agent is engine "runner", so any new room takes this path. Two back-to-back room creations — very likely with judges/teammates tonight — hard-fail the second room even though a slot frees up minutes later. The finding's mechanism, line numbers, and failure scenario all hold; the only mitigation is that once A reaches "ready" it becomes an LRU suspension candidate, but that does not cover the multi-minute provisioning window where back-to-back creations occur.

summary: A slow LRU/retry suspend blocks the serialized capacity queue — and therefore ALL room provisioning — for up to ~16 minutes (statusWaitAttempts 24 x up to 40s per request).
failure_scenario: suspendRecord runs inside serializeCapacity (every provision for every room queues behind capacityQueue at lines 494-498). If the Runloop suspend is slow or the devbox is stuck transitioning, waitForDevbox at line 471 loops up to 24 attempts, each a POST with a 30s server-side wait and 40s client timeout. One misbehaving suspend stalls provisioning of every other room for many minutes — indistinguishable from a hang on stage.
suggested_fix: Suspends normally complete in seconds: pass a much smaller attempt budget for the suspend path (e.g. 4 attempts), or perform only the suspend POST inside the serialized section and do the waitForDevbox confirmation outside the capacity queue (optimistically mark the record inactive once the POST is accepted).

verdict.reason: Verified in /Users/kingroy/claude/hackathon/ensemble/server/provision.mjs: suspendRecord (called at lines 504/527) runs inside serializeCapacity, and every provision for every room serializes on the single capacityQueue (lines 494-498, 501). If the suspend POST (line 467) does not return status "suspended", waitForDevbox (line 471) loops up to statusWaitAttempts=24 attempts, each a wait_for_status POST with a 30s server-side hold that returns 408 while the devbox is still "suspending" — and 408 is swallowed and retried (line 351). So one slow/stuck suspend blocks ALL room provisioning, and provisionInternal emits no status event until reserveCapacity resolves (first report is line 587), so blocked users see nothing — a hang on stage. The trigger is realistic tonight: maxLive defaults to 2 with a pinned demo workspace excluded from suspension, so the LRU suspend fires on nearly every provision beyond capacity, and these devboxes have heavy disk state (npm install) making non-instant suspends the common path. One correction: the worst case is ~12 minutes (24 x 30s server hold), not ~16 — the 40s client timeout throws a TimeoutError, not RunloopRequestError 408, so it terminates the loop (line 352) rather than multiplying it. The corrected bound does not refute the finding; multi-minute global stalls, and routine tens-of-seconds stalls with zero feedback, genuinely hold.

summary: LRU-suspended devboxes are orphaned forever: re-provisioning the room replaces the record (records.set) and drops the suspended devboxId — it is never resumed, released, or shut down.
failure_scenario: Room A gets LRU-suspended when room B provisions. User returns to room A: the record is inactive so provisionInternal falls through to reserveCapacity, which creates a brand-new devbox and overwrites the record at line 544, discarding the suspended devbox's id. The suspended devbox persists on the Runloop account indefinitely (suspend != shutdown), accumulating one orphan per eviction/revisit cycle over the night — cost leak plus creeping toward account devbox caps. Bonus pain: the user waits through a full multi-minute re-provision when a resume would take seconds.
suggested_fix: In reserveCapacity, when the room's existing record is inactive with status 'suspended', either resume it (POST devboxes/{id}/resume, then wait running) instead of creating a new devbox, or at minimum fire a shutdown for the old suspended devboxId before records.set replaces it.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by code trace. suspendRecord (provision.mjs:458) sets active=false but keeps the devbox suspended on Runloop; provisionInternal's reuse branches (lines 553/572) both require existing.active, so a revisited suspended room falls through to reserveCapacity, which overwrites the record at line 544 and creates a new devbox — the suspended devboxId becomes unreachable. No resume call exists anywhere in the codebase; release() only runs on room deletion and would target the new record; the caller's onSuspend handler (index.js:757) just clears runnerUrl and emits status. The trigger is likely tonight: maxLive=2 and the pinned demo room counts toward activeRecords while being un-evictable, leaving one slot, so two audience rooms alternating will cycle evict/revisit — each cycle orphans a devbox AND forces a multi-minute full re-provision mid-demo. Caveats: suspended devboxes bill storage not compute, so the overnight dollar leak is small, and keep_alive_time_seconds=14400 may bound lifetimes; the demo-visible cost is mainly the repeated multi-minute re-provision that a resume path would avoid.

summary: close() aborts requests but never suspends/shuts down active non-pinned devboxes — every server restart or redeploy leaks up to maxLive running devboxes for 4 hours.
failure_scenario: Hackathon workflow tonight involves repeated redeploys of the hub. Each close()/process exit leaves the currently-active devboxes (up to 2) running until keep_alive expiry; five redeploys during the evening can leave ~10 devbox-hours of orphaned compute and eat into the Runloop account devbox cap, which then makes fresh provisions fail during the actual demo.
suggested_fix: In close(), after awaiting inflight, iterate activeRecords(), skip pinned, and issue best-effort `POST devboxes/{id}/suspend` for each with a short per-request timeout (do NOT route through the already-aborted closeController signal — use a fresh AbortSignal.timeout).

verdict.reason: Confirmed in provision.mjs: close() (lines 839-844) only aborts inflight requests — it never suspends or shuts down active devboxes, which are created with keep_alive_time_seconds=14400 (4h, line 595) and capped at maxLive=2 concurrent. Devbox IDs exist only in the in-memory records map, so a restarted process cannot reclaim orphans; it provisions fresh boxes for the same rooms. The server's only cleanup path (release() -> devboxes/{id}/shutdown in index.js line 1495) runs solely on explicit room deletion, and the SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown hook delegates entirely to provisioner.close(). So every graceful redeploy tonight orphans up to 2 running devboxes for up to 4 hours; repeated redeploys accumulate orphaned devbox-hours that count against the Runloop concurrent-devbox cap and can make fresh provisions fail during the demo. The fix's caveat is also correct: apiRequest throws when closed=true (line 311) and every request is bound to closeController.signal (lines 302-308), so cleanup must use a fresh AbortSignal.timeout and bypass the closed check.

summary: state_v2.json is written only after every deploy step succeeds; any failure after devbox creation (lines 92, 112) orphans one or two devboxes with open tunnels for 8 hours, and --teardown can't find them because state still holds the previous deploy's ids.
failure_scenario: npm install or a health wait fails on the hub (line 119/137) after the workspace devbox and hub devbox were already created. Script exits; state_v2.json is stale; `--teardown` shuts down the OLD ids. Operator re-runs deploy, creating more boxes. Repeated retries before the demo exhaust the Runloop account cap (the same cap SPEC-V2's max-2-workspaces guard exists to protect), so in-demo room provisioning starts failing on stage.
suggested_fix: Persist incrementally: merge {"demo_ws_id": ws.id} into state_v2.json immediately after each create() (before any install/health step), and/or wrap main() in try/except that shuts down every devbox created in this run on failure. Teardown can additionally sweep rl.devboxes.list for running boxes named ensemble-*.

verdict.reason: Verified in /Users/kingroy/claude/hackathon/ensemble/deploy/deploy_v2.py: state_v2.json is written only at line 147 as the very last step of main(), with no try/except and no incremental persistence. Failure-prone steps (run_long npm installs at lines 104/119, wait_http_ok at 106/137 — all of which raise) sit between devbox creation (lines 92, 112) and the state write, so a failure there orphans 1-2 devboxes with keep_alive=8h (line 21); in the hub-failure cases the workspace tunnel is already open with auth_mode="open" (line 107) and the codex auth.json on the box. --teardown (lines 63-72) shuts down only the ids stored in state — the previous deploy's — and has no list/sweep by name, so it cannot find the orphans (and crashes on a missing state file). The account-cap consequence is corroborated: docs/SPEC-V2.md line 46 cites "demo safety under account caps" and server/provision.mjs enforces DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE_WORKSPACES=2, but deploy orphans count against the same account limit outside that guard, so repeated pre-demo retry failures can make in-demo room provisioning fail. Mitigations (ids printed to stdout, dashboard cleanup, 8h auto-expiry) are manual or too slow for tonight and do not refute the defect.
